la-aurora--la-aurora-100-anos.description: Created for La Aurora's centenary, 100 Años is a Dominican puro: wrapper, binder and filler all come from the Cibao Valley. It is a strong, layered smoke where leather, wood and bitter cocoa meet a honeyed, nutty sweetness, and the strength builds steadily towards the end.

thirds.notes: Mocha, leather and cedar spice open, with the cocoa turning darker and a hint of citrus behind it.
Pepper steps forward beside the chocolate, and nuts start to join the citrus in the background.
Nuts, citrus and pepper lead to the end, over a base of chocolate and leather.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – La Aurora Cien Años review

la-aurora--la-aurora-107-ecuador.description: Released for the factory's 107th year, this member of the Tobaccos of the World series pairs a sun-grown Ecuadorian wrapper with a Cibao Valley binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. It starts gently with a little spice, then gathers strength around cocoa, leather and wood, with a sweet edge from the oily, reddish leaf.

thirds.notes: Sweet orange citrus on the tongue, soon joined by leather and black pepper on the finish.
Wood arrives at the midpoint and shares the lead with leather as the sweetness recedes.
A buttery smoothness rounds off the last section, with citrus and pepper lingering behind.

la-aurora--la-aurora-107-maduro.description: The dark member of the 107 family dresses the regular blend in a silky Broadleaf maduro wrapper from the United States, over a Cibao Valley binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. Wood and spice lead at first, then dark chocolate, earth and toasted nuts take over, with a natural sweetness from the leaf.

thirds.notes: Woody and spiced, with a caramel-like sweetness carried by the dark wrapper.
Dark chocolate and earth deepen, a creamy texture builds and pepper shows on the retrohale.
Roasted nuts and a touch of hay join in as the flavours open up towards the band.

sources.title: Cigar Reviews by the Katman – La Aurora 107 Maduro

la-aurora--la-aurora-107-usa.description: La Aurora's name for the 107 dressed in a Broadleaf maduro wrapper grown in the United States, with a binder from the Cibao Valley instead of the Ecuadorian leaf of the regular 107. Filler comes from the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Peru. The maker describes a medium-full smoke: woody and spiced at first, sweet on the tongue, with toasted and nutty notes.

la-aurora--la-aurora-107-nicaragua.description: A Nicaraguan puro rolled at La Aurora in Santiago, part of the 107 Tobaccos of the World series: wrapper, binder and filler all come from Nicaragua. It opens spicy with a touch of leather, then settles into earth, wood and nuts, with a floral retrohale and a licorice-like note near the finish.

thirds.notes: Baking spice, leather and a mix of black and red pepper over an earthy base.
Earth, wood and nutty tones hold steady while the pepper slowly climbs.
Pepper moves to the front, a licorice hint appears and the retrohale turns floral.

sources.title: Bespoke Unit – La Aurora 107 Nicaragua review

la-aurora--la-aurora-115-aniversario.description: Made to mark 115 years of La Aurora, this blend sets an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Brazilian binder, with filler from the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Brazil. Black pepper leads the way in, creamy wood runs through the whole smoke, and cinnamon, walnut and a citrus echo arrive towards a firmer finish.

thirds.notes: Wood with an edge, black pepper on the retrohale and a sweet, cherry-like note behind.
The wood stays in front and takes on a light char, as the sweetness and pepper ease off.
Pepper returns to meet the wood, with nutty and citrus touches at the close.

la-aurora--la-aurora-120-aniversario.description: Released for the company's 120th year, this Dominican puro wears a Habano '92 wrapper over an Olor binder, with Piloto Cubano, Olor and Corojo filler from the Cibao Valley; each cigar comes in a cedar sleeve. Spice and pepper meet wood at the start, coffee and cocoa follow, and sweeter, earthier notes close it out.

thirds.notes: Strong cedar from the first draw, with spice, red pepper on the retrohale and a dry, hay-like tang.
Oak, a candied citrus note and milky coffee join in, over a quiet leather base.
Sweeter and woodier, with earth and hints of raisin and vanilla to the finish.

la-aurora--preferidos-1903-edition.description: Preferidos is La Aurora's family of figurados, named after the factory's first brand from 1903. Each version has its own blend and wrapper (Connecticut, Brazilian maduro, Ecuador, Cameroon, Broadleaf, Corojo and others) around Dominican tobacco from the Cibao Valley. The perfecto shape is slow work: one roller makes about a hundred a day.

la-aurora--cameroon-1903.description: One of La Aurora's Original Blends, Cameroon 1903 takes its name from the wrapper seed, now grown in Ecuador, set over an Ecuadorian binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. It comes in a wide range of sizes. Expect a medium smoke of sweet cinnamon spice, mocha and wood, with a touch of red-fruit brightness.

thirds.notes: Mocha and wood lead with gentle sweetness, while cedar and mixed pepper show on the retrohale.
The mocha leans more towards coffee, with pepper and earth in the background.
A light bitterness balances the sweet coffee as the strength edges upward.

la-aurora--corojo-1962.description: Part of La Aurora's Original Blends, Corojo 1962 swaps in an Ecuadorian-grown Corojo wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder, with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Creamy roasted coffee and light spice sit on a base of wood and nuts, with floral, leather and honey notes; the strength runs from medium towards full.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – 1962 Corojo Robusto review
Blind Man's Puff – La Aurora 1962 Corojo Robusto

thirds.notes: Wood and red pepper with a cocoa-like sweetness, a touch of cinnamon and an earthy finish.
Cedar and earth lead, with salted nuts, cocoa and espresso, and pepper on the retrohale.
Mostly woody, at times bitter, while a cherry note and a vanilla finish appear for some.

la-aurora--connecticut-1987.description: The Connecticut-wrapped member of La Aurora's Original Blends: a light brown Ecuadorian Connecticut leaf over an Ecuadorian binder, with Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. Leather and cedar set the tone, while a smooth, creamy smoke carries nuts, cocoa and gentle sweetness. A calm choice for the morning or an unhurried afternoon.

thirds.notes: A clear nuttiness with hay and grain, a creamy finish and a little pepper on the retrohale.
Slightly earthier, with growing grain notes and an occasional licorice touch.
Still smooth to the end, with butterscotch sweetness, nuts and a hint of licorice.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – 1987 Connecticut Toro review

la-aurora--maduro-1985.description: The fourth of La Aurora's Original Blends: a Brazilian maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It starts with mineral earth and light pepper, then shows almond, sweet nuts and dark chocolate, with baking spice running through and a fruit-tinged finish. A medium, approachable maduro for the evening.

thirds.notes: Cinnamon and nutmeg over mineral earth, with a light pepper touch.
More subdued: cedar and baking spice, a hint of caramel and chocolate on the finish.
A darker, licorice-like edge arrives while the spice lingers on the palate.

la-aurora--adn-dominicano.description: ADN Dominicano puts Andullo in the filler: a Dominican tobacco pressed and fermented in tightly bound palm-bark rolls. Around it sit Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler, a Cameroon binder and a Cibao Valley wrapper. Spice and wood come first, then a natural sweetness and a bready, graham-cracker finish.

thirds.notes: Musty wood, black pepper and a grassy note, with cedar on the retrohale.
Sweet natural tobacco with a tart, apple-like fruit; the mustiness fades.
Bready, graham-like sweetness takes over while the pepper grows on the tongue.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – ADN Dominicano Toro review

la-aurora--cazadores-claro.description: Cazadores is La Aurora's everyday range, made in the Dominican Republic with Dominican filler from the Cibao Valley and an Indonesian binder. The Claro wears an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and smokes mild to medium, creamy and mellow, with notes of oak, earth and a light citrus touch.

la-aurora--cazadores-maduro.description: The dark version of La Aurora's everyday Cazadores range pairs an Indonesian maduro wrapper and Indonesian binder with Dominican filler from the Cibao Valley. A medium smoke with roasted nuts, cedar and earth, a gentle cocoa undertone and a creamy finish.

la-aurora--cazadores-nicaragua.description: The Nicaraguan-wrapped version of La Aurora's everyday Cazadores range: a sun-grown Nicaraguan wrapper over an Indonesian binder and Dominican filler from the Cibao Valley. It is a medium smoke, livelier than its siblings, with black pepper, toasted wood, hay and an earthy nuttiness.

la-aurora--especiales.description: Especiales was blended by Manuel Inoa over several years with feedback from a large group of retailers. A reddish, Ecuadorian-grown Cameroon wrapper covers a Dominican binder and Dominican and U.S. filler. It is a medium, creamy smoke with spiced oak and a candy-like sweetness, moving on to cashew, coffee, hay and citrus peel.

la-aurora--excepcionales.description: Excepcionales uses Habana Corojo leaf for both wrapper and binder, over Dominican filler, and La Aurora makes only a small lot each year. The maker describes a balanced smoke moving from medium to full, built on wood, with creamy roasted coffee, steady spice and a nutty touch of hazelnut and walnut.

la-aurora--1495-series.description: Aimed at experienced smokers, the 1495 Series blends six tobaccos from five countries: a dark, oily Ecuadorian wrapper, a Brazilian binder and filler from the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Brazil and Peru. Black pepper and earth lead, wood stays present throughout, and cinnamon, nuts and a creamy finish follow.

thirds.notes: Earth on the tongue with pepper on the finish, and coffee joining early on.
Past the first third the pepper grows and moves from the finish into the main draw.
Pepper and wood hold to the end, with some spice and a smooth, creamy close.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – La Aurora 1495 Series review

la-aurora--hors-d-age.description: A limited Preferidos release in which twelve years pass from planting the seed to rolling the cigar. Ecuadorian wrapper and binder cover filler from Colombia, the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua, and each edition appears in a single new size. Chocolate opens, then wood and earth take the lead, with pepper and baking spice to finish.

thirds.notes: Chocolate moves to the front over earth, wood and red pepper.
Wood and earth take the lead as the chocolate recedes and pepper grows.
Earth and wood stay in front, with pepper and baking spice close behind.

sources.title: La Aurora – Hors d'Âge Limited Edition
Cigar Coop – Hors d'Age Salomon review

la-aurora--family-creed-fuerte-sol.description: The first release in La Aurora's Family Creed series, named after the León family's guiding principles. This box-pressed blend uses a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper, a Nicaraguan binder and filler from the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Pennsylvania. Leather, earth and cedar meet mulled spice and dark fruit, growing sweeter and more floral midway.

thirds.notes: Leather, mineral earth and resinous cedar, with a mulled-wine touch of fruit and clove.
Salty cedar and a tea-like note; the blend turns more floral and gains sweetness.
Spicier retrohales, dark fruit and soil and oak for a firm finish.

sources.title: Klaro Cigars – Family Creed Fuerte Sol review
70cigars – La Aurora Family Creed Fuerte Sol

la-aurora--family-creed-perseverancia.description: The second Family Creed release, launched in 2026: a box-pressed blend with a Pennsylvania Broadleaf wrapper over a Mexican San Andrés binder, and filler from Pennsylvania, the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. Despite the dark leaf it opens lighter than expected, with leather, cedar, green peppercorn and hazelnut, then settles on coffee and cream.

sources.title: Cigar Reviews by the Katman – Family Creed Perseverancia

la-aurora--stravaganza.description: Stravaganza by La Aurora combines an Ecuadorian wrapper and binder with filler from the Dominican Cibao Valley. The maker describes red fruit and wood with a citrus touch, along with nuts and a rich, creamy coffee note.
